title: switch-case statement
concept: The role of switch statements and breaks to branch by comparing one value to multiple cases

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation:
**`int main() {`** — The starting point of the program, the main stack frame is created on the stack.

In this lesson you will learn the **switch-case statement**.

steps.title: Initializing day variable
steps.explanation: **`int day = 3;`** — Declare an integer variable `day` and initialize it to **3**. 1 means Monday, 2 means Tuesday, and 3 means Wednesday.

steps.title: Switch statement entry
steps.explanation: **`switch (day) {`** — Compares the value in parentheses (`day = 3`) with the value in each case from top to bottom. If a matching case is found, the code is executed from that point.

steps.title: case 3 match - output
steps.explanation: **`printf("Wednesday\n");`** — Since the value **3** of `day` matched `case 3:`, the switch jumps to this point and executes the code. `Wednesday` is displayed on the screen.

steps.title: Escape from switch with break
steps.explanation: **`break;`** — An escape command that **immediately exits** a switch statement. When a break is encountered, it moves directly to the line following the closing `}` of the switch.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation: **`return 0;`** — The program terminates normally after exiting the switch. As main's stack frame is freed, `day` also disappears from memory.

quiz.explanation:
If there is no break, fall-through occurs.
Starting from case 1, all code below it (case 2, case 3, default) is executed sequentially.
Therefore, A, B, C, and D are all output.

misconceptions.correct: If there is no break, all code from the matching case down is executed continuously (fall-through).
misconceptions.why: A switch only 'jumps' and does not automatically stop. break is an explicit termination signal.

keyTakeaway: The switch jumps to the case where the value matches, and if there is no break, it falls through.
